To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gamification can be applied to medical image segmentation via crowd workers.

gamified crowdsourcing can be used for medical image segmentation tasks and that a combination of different gamification incentives can be applied to achieve a high quality segmentation while keeping users motivated.

gamification of medical image segmentation can be achieved via (a) a points scoring system that rewards users instantly for accurate segmentation, (b) a leaderboard ranking system that lets users accumulate points for long-term motivation, (c ) a badge achievement system that provides a visual representation of the user's "strength" in the segmentation task, and (d ) a level system that visualizes the learning curve of the user in performing the image segmentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
gamification of image segmentation as a crowdsourcing task.
the development of a game concept for medical image annotation that is suitable for a crowd and that can be integrated into existing crowdsourcing platforms such as Amazon Mechanical Turk.
the development of gamification concepts for medical image segmentation via crowd sourcing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gamification can be a valuable tool for crowdsourcing medical image segmentation.
gamification is not a silver bullet and that the concept has to be adapted to the specific task at hand.
gamification is an interesting approach to motivate users in crowdsourcing medical image segmentation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gamification is a promising approach to motivate crowd workers for performing medical image segmentation tasks.
we propose a gamification concept for medical image annotation that is based on a combination of the incentives (a) points, (b) leaderboards, (c) badge achievements and (d) level progression.
we propose a game concept to motivate crowd workers for medical image segmentation and that the game concept compliess with the guidelines from prior work.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gamification concept for medical image annotation can be implemented in a straightforward way, and the concept is compatible with the previously proposed crowdsourcing concept.
gamification of medical image segmentation can be achieved by combining the presented incentives.
gamification can be applied for the acquisition of annotations in medical image segmentation.
